title: post_save signal never fires for proxy-model admin saves — cache staleness up to 5 min on every admin write
description: The signal is registered as @receiver(post_save, sender=SiteSettings). Django dispatches post_save with sender=self.__class__, which for all 8 proxy admin tabs (SiteSettingsBranding, SiteSettingsSEO, SiteSettingsNavigation, SiteSettingsHomepage, SiteSettingsContact, SiteSettingsTelegram, SiteSettingsEmoji, SiteSettingsEditorial) is the proxy class — not SiteSettings. The handler is never called, so the cache key 'site_settings_singleton' is never deleted, and the live site serves stale configuration for the full 5-minute TTL after every admin save. Since the direct SiteSettings tab is never used in practice (admin is partitioned into proxy tabs), cache invalidation is effectively dead for all normal admin usage.
verdict_note: Confirmed in services.py:55 and models.py:912-965. Eight proxy classes defined, signal sender only matches concrete SiteSettings. Cache invalidation is dead for all proxy admin saves.

title: bleach fallback branch applies no style restrictions when CSSSanitizer is unavailable
description: When the try/except ImportError at line 24 caches css_sanitizer=None, the else-branch at line 42 checks `if int(bleach.__version__.split('.')[0]) < 6`. With bleach==6.2.0 pinned this condition is always False, so bleach.clean() is called with neither css_sanitizer= nor styles= when the fallback path executes. In that scenario bleach 6.x emits NoCssSanitizerWarning and passes inline style attribute values through unchecked, allowing arbitrary CSS. The fallback is dormant under normal packaging but silently broken rather than failing loudly.
suggested_fix:
Delete the else-branch entirely (it can never execute with pinned bleach 6.2.0). In the except ImportError block, raise ImproperlyConfigured instead of caching None, to make the failure visible at startup:

```python
try:
    from bleach.css_sanitizer import CSSSanitizer
    css_sanitizer = CSSSanitizer(allowed_css_properties=ALLOWED_STYLES)
except ImportError:
    from django.core.exceptions import ImproperlyConfigured
    raise ImproperlyConfigured('bleach CSSSanitizer is required; install bleach>=6')
```
verdict_note: Confirmed in utils.py:24-50. The version check on line 47 evaluates to False for bleach 6.2.0 (6 < 6 is False). When ImportError fires, bleach.clean() runs with no style restriction at all.

title: WebP magic-byte check matches 4-byte RIFF prefix only — WAV files pass; .webp extension bypasses check entirely
description: IMAGE_MAGIC_BYTES maps b'RIFF' (4 bytes) to 'webp', but the RIFF container is shared with WAV audio. A WAV renamed to .jpg passes the magic check (valid_magic=True). Additionally, the guard at line 116 places '.webp' in a bypass set, meaning WebP files skip the magic check entirely — the 12-byte WEBP identifier at bytes 8-12 is never verified. PIL img.verify() downstream mitigates both issues for corrupt files, but the magic-byte layer provides weaker assurance than intended. Upload endpoint is staff-only.
verdict_note: Confirmed in views.py:23-29 (RIFF 4-byte entry) and line 116 (.webp in bypass set). PIL verify() is the effective guard, reducing this to a defence-in-depth gap.

title: SVG sanitizer misses <animateMotion> — XSS vector via xlink:href not stripped
description: _SVG_DANGEROUS_TAG_GROUP at line 36 matches animate(?:Transform)? but not animateMotion. The <animateMotion> element can carry xlink:href or href pointing to javascript: URIs and has appeared in SVG XSS payloads. _SVG_XLINK_HREF_JS at line 49 strips javascript: hrefs as attributes but only when they appear as direct attributes — not inside animateMotion child mpath elements. Upload is staff-only, reducing exploitability.
suggested_fix:
Extend the group to include animateMotion:

```python
_SVG_DANGEROUS_TAG_GROUP = r'(?:script|foreignObject|set|animate(?:Transform|Motion)?)'
```
verdict_note: Confirmed in views.py:36. animateMotion is absent from the group. _SVG_XLINK_HREF_JS does strip javascript: hrefs as direct attributes but animateMotion element-level removal is missing.

title: X-Forwarded-For IP spoofing bypasses admin IP restriction and contact rate limit
description: Both AdminIPRestrictionMiddleware._get_ip() (security_middleware.py:141-145) and spam_protection._get_client_ip() (contact/spam_protection.py:51-56) blindly trust the first value of the client-controlled HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR header. An attacker can send X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1 to appear as a whitelisted IP, bypassing admin IP restriction entirely. The same spoofing defeats the contact form rate limit by rotating IPs per request (20 unique IPs = 20 submissions before any key is exhausted). Nginx is the reverse proxy and sets REMOTE_ADDR to the real client IP.
verdict_note: Confirmed in security_middleware.py:111-114 and 141-145, and contact/spam_protection.py:51-56. All three helpers trust raw XFF. prod.py:58 confirms Nginx is the single trusted proxy — REMOTE_ADDR is sufficient.

title: AdminIPRestrictionMiddleware silently no-ops when ADMIN_ALLOWED_IPS is absent from .env
description: The guard at line 129 is `if self.allowed_ips and ...`, treating an empty list as 'no restriction'. base.py:213 defaults ADMIN_ALLOWED_IPS to []. prod.py does not set or assert this variable. If the .env file omits ADMIN_ALLOWED_IPS, the entire admin IP restriction is silently disabled — the admin panel is publicly reachable at the custom admin URL with no IP gate.
suggested_fix:
Add a startup assertion in prod.py or in AdminIPRestrictionMiddleware.__init__:

```python
# In prod.py
assert env.list('ADMIN_ALLOWED_IPS', default=[]), \
    'ADMIN_ALLOWED_IPS must be set to a non-empty list in production'
```

Alternatively, invert the default to 'block all' by treating empty list as deny-all: `if not self.allowed_ips or client_ip not in self.allowed_ips:` and block unconditionally when `allowed_ips` is empty.
verdict_note: Confirmed in security_middleware.py:129 (if self.allowed_ips guard), base.py:213 (default=[]), and prod.py (no ADMIN_ALLOWED_IPS assertion). Empty env var = fully open admin.

title: Contact DRF endpoint has no per-action throttle — rate limit bypasses SSR spam protection
description: ContactMessageViewSet.create is opened to AllowAny via get_permissions() but no throttle_classes override is set. It inherits the global AnonRateThrottle of 20/min (base.py) / 20/min (prod.py:88). The SSR contact view enforces a stricter 3-per-600s per-IP rate limit via spam_protection.py. A bot that POSTs JSON directly to /api/contact/ bypasses honeypot and spam_protection entirely, subject only to the global anon throttle — 20 contact messages per minute per IP.
verdict_note: Confirmed in api/views.py:110-121 (no throttle_classes). base.py:253-260 and prod.py:85-91 show global anon rate of 20-30/min. SSR spam protection at 3/600s is not enforced for the API path.

title: SiteSettingsSerializer exposes Telegram owner ID and verification tokens to all Django admin users
description: SiteSettingsSerializer.Meta.exclude only omits file fields and timestamps. telegram_owner_id, telegram_admin_group_id, telegram_channel_id, google_site_verification, yandex_verification, bing_verification, and all 100+ tg_emoji_* fields are serialized in GET /api/site-settings/ responses. The endpoint is IsAdminUser so this is admin-only, but any Django staff user with admin login can read the owner's personal Telegram numeric ID and all verification tokens even if their role has no access to SiteSettings in the Unfold panel.
suggested_fix: Replace the exclude-based serializer with an explicit fields list containing only values a legitimate consumer needs (branding, SEO meta text, editorial copy). At minimum add telegram_owner_id, telegram_admin_group_id, telegram_channel_id, all tg_emoji_* fields, google_site_verification, yandex_verification, and bing_verification to the exclude tuple. Since SSR templates use the context processor for site settings, consider whether this endpoint has any current legitimate caller.
verdict_note: Confirmed in serializers.py:131-134. Exclude list is narrow (file fields + timestamps only). All Telegram IDs and verification tokens serialize. Endpoint is IsAdminUser, limiting exposure to authenticated staff.

title: Duplicated _get_ip helper in RequestSanitizationMiddleware and AdminIPRestrictionMiddleware
description: The identical 4-line _get_ip(self, request) method is defined in both RequestSanitizationMiddleware (lines 110-114) and AdminIPRestrictionMiddleware (lines 141-145). Any future fix to IP extraction logic (e.g. switching from XFF to REMOTE_ADDR per the XFF spoofing finding) must be applied in both places. No class state is used, so neither needs to be a method.
verdict_note: Confirmed in security_middleware.py:110-114 and 141-145. Identical 4-line bodies. contact/spam_protection.py has a third copy (_get_client_ip at line 51) with the same logic.

title: SiteSettings.load() called directly in 4 places, bypassing the 5-minute cache
description: custom_404_view (line 34), custom_500_view (line 46), _apps_visible() (line 86), and dashboard_callback() (dashboard.py:94) all call SiteSettings.load() — a get_or_create(pk=1) DB round-trip — instead of SiteSettingsService.get() which adds the 5-minute cache. The context processor correctly uses SiteSettingsService.get(). _apps_visible() is called on every dispatch of ProjectListView and ProjectDetailView, issuing an uncached DB query on every project page render.
verdict_note: Confirmed in views.py:34, 46, 86 and dashboard.py:94. All four call SiteSettings.load() directly. Context processor (context_processors.py:24) correctly uses SiteSettingsService.get().

title: Bleach allowlist constants duplicated between core/utils.py and blog/markdown_extras.py with diverging tag sets
description: core/utils.py defines ALLOWED_TAGS (22 elements) and ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES as the canonical rich-text bleach allowlist. markdown_extras.py defines its own independent ALLOWED_TAGS (27 elements) and ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES. The two lists differ: markdown_extras adds del, ins, mark, abbr; core/utils.py misses those but they are intentional for markdown. More critically, markdown_extras.py omits `style` from ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES (safer), while core allows style on all elements. A security tightening that removes a tag from core's list will silently miss the markdown rendering path.
verdict_note: Confirmed in markdown_extras.py:16-39. Lists intentionally differ (markdown vs rich-text use cases). markdown_extras is actually more restrictive (no style). Primary risk is maintenance drift; not a security bug today.

description: ticker_items_resolved, manifesto_principles_resolved, process_steps_resolved, team_values_resolved, and footer_practice_items_resolved (lines 872-889) each implement `return self.X if self.X else _default_X()`. Five top-level module functions exist only to be called from these properties. Adding a sixth JSON list field requires remembering to add both the default function and this property pattern.
verdict_note: Confirmed in models.py:872-889. Five identical-shape properties. Purely a readability nit with no correctness impact.

title: Four footer_display_ properties repeat the same field-fallback pattern
description: footer_display_github, footer_display_linkedin, footer_display_twitter, footer_display_telegram (lines 892-905) each implement `return self.footer_social_X or self.X_url`. The pattern is correct and clear, but any change to the fallback logic must be applied four times.
suggested_fix: Minor: add a single-line helper `def _footer_url(self, override, canonical): return getattr(self, override) or getattr(self, canonical)` and reduce each property to one line. Lowest-priority nit — code is correct as-is.
verdict_note: Confirmed in models.py:892-905. Four identical-shape properties. Correct code, style-only nit.

title: TelegramEntity fetched with uncached DB query on every request for logged-in Telegram users
description: The site_settings context processor runs on every template render. For any Telegram-authenticated user (tg_profile_id in session), it executes TelegramEntity.objects.get(pk=profile_id) with no caching. This is an unguarded DB round-trip per page view per authenticated user. With 3 Gunicorn sync workers, authenticated traffic exhausts worker slots on DB I/O under any moderate load.
suggested_fix:
Cache the TelegramEntity lookup by session key with a short TTL:

```python
from django.core.cache import cache

profile_id = request.session.get('tg_profile_id')
if profile_id:
    cache_key = f'tg_profile_{profile_id}'
    tg_profile = cache.get(cache_key)
    if tg_profile is None:
        try:
            from telegram.models import TelegramEntity
            tg_profile = TelegramEntity.objects.get(pk=profile_id)
            cache.set(cache_key, tg_profile, 300)  # 5 min
        except TelegramEntity.DoesNotExist:
            request.session.pop('tg_profile_id', None)
```
verdict_note: Confirmed in context_processors.py:15-21. No caching around TelegramEntity.objects.get(pk=profile_id). Fires on every request for Telegram-authenticated users.

title: HomeView issues two sequential DB queries where one suffices — redundant exists() before first()
description: At line 157-160, Case 2 (no cookie but IP already seen) runs PageView.objects.filter(ip_address=ip).exists() and then, in the next line, PageView.objects.filter(ip_address=ip).first(). The exists() check is redundant: .first() returns None when no record exists, so the outcome of both calls is the same. This is two DB round-trips where one suffices on every home-page visit from a returning IP-known incognito browser.
suggested_fix:
Collapse to a single query:

```python
existing = PageView.objects.filter(ip_address=ip).first() if ip else None
if existing:
    response.set_cookie(
        self.VISITOR_COOKIE, str(existing.visitor_id),
        max_age=self.COOKIE_MAX_AGE, httponly=True, samesite='Lax',
    )
else:
    # Case 3: genuinely new visitor
    ...
```
verdict_note: Confirmed in views.py:157-160. The elif branch calls .exists() on line 157 then .first() on line 160 with identical filter — two round-trips for the same result.

title: SiteSettings.visitor_count property is dead code that duplicates the HomeView cache key
description: SiteSettings.visitor_count property (models.py:850-857) uses cache key 'visitor_count' and calls PageView.objects.count(). HomeView.get_context_data (views.py:24-130) uses the identical cache key 'visitor_count' and the same PageView.objects.count() call. No template reads site_settings.visitor_count — templates receive visitor_count from the HomeView context directly. The property is unreachable and shares a cache key with the authoritative HomeView implementation.
suggested_fix: Remove the visitor_count property from SiteSettings entirely. The single canonical implementation in HomeView is sufficient. If visitor_count ever needs to be available site-wide (e.g. footer), move the caching logic into a standalone function in core/services.py.
verdict_note: Confirmed in models.py:850-857 and views.py:24-130. Same 'visitor_count' cache key. No template or code path calls site_settings.visitor_count — confirmed by grep showing no site_settings.visitor_count references outside the model file itself.

title: SQL_PATTERNS regex compiled at import but never applied — intended SQL injection check is silently absent
description: RequestSanitizationMiddleware defines SQL_PATTERNS = re.compile(...) at lines 49-53 covering UNION/SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP/ALTER/CREATE/EXEC. The regex is never referenced in __call__ or any other method — only NULL_BYTE and PATH_TRAVERSAL are actually applied. The SQL injection check is dead code. The intended protection is absent, and reviewers reading the middleware may assume SQL patterns are being checked.
suggested_fix: Remove SQL_PATTERNS entirely. Django's ORM uses parameterised queries, making URL-level SQL pattern scanning both insufficient (it misses POST body injection) and high false-positive (legitimate search terms like 'select' or 'drop' in slugs). If removal feels wrong, at minimum add SQL_PATTERNS.search to __call__ and wire it to the same HttpResponseForbidden path as NULL_BYTE.
verdict_note: Confirmed in security_middleware.py:49-53 and __call__ (lines 70-108). SQL_PATTERNS is defined but .search() is never called anywhere in the class.

title: setup_rbac references removed botproxy and osint apps — misleading dead code runs on every deploy
description: create_rbac_groups() queries for permissions with content_type__app_label='botproxy' (line 35) and content_type__app_label='osint' (line 41-45). Both apps were removed. Neither directory exists under apps/. The queries return empty QuerySets and the if-perm guards make them no-ops, but the code misleads readers into believing botproxy and osint permissions exist. The post_migrate signal wires this to run on every deploy.
suggested_fix: Remove lines 33-45 (the botproxy and osint permission lookup blocks) and update the analyst group comment on line 23 to remove OSINT references. If the analyst group needs real permissions from current apps, add them explicitly.
verdict_note: Confirmed in setup_rbac.py:35-45. Neither apps/botproxy nor apps/osint directories exist. if-guards make it a safe no-op, but code is dead and misleading.

title: tg_emoji_osint admin fieldset labeled 'OSINT' — orphaned label from removed app, though field still has live callers
description: tg_emoji_osint CharField exists on TelegramMixin (models.py:414) and 'osint' appears in emoji.py _ALL_FIELDS (line 24) and emoji_views.py EMOJI_FIELDS (line 58). The osint app was removed. However, interactions/notifications/service.py:187 and 192 still call ce('osint', ...) for EntitySource records with service='osint' — so the emoji field itself has live callers. The admin.py fieldset labeled 'OSINT' (admin.py:354) is the stale artefact: it groups tg_emoji_channel_icon and related fields under an 'OSINT' header that no longer reflects their actual use.
suggested_fix: Rename the admin fieldset from 'OSINT' to 'Telegram Log Emojis' or 'Entity Log Emojis' in admin.py:354. The tg_emoji_osint field itself can remain since service.py still uses the 'osint' key. Optionally rename the emoji key from 'osint' to 'entity_source' and update service.py accordingly to remove the OSINT terminology.
verdict_note: Confirmed in models.py:414, admin.py:354, emoji.py:24, and interactions/notifications/service.py:187,192. Field has live callers — not purely dead. The misleading 'OSINT' admin label is the real issue.

title: serialize_comment crashes with ValueError when comment.image has no file
description: Line 502: `getattr(comment, 'image', None) and hasattr(comment.image, 'url')` is always truthy for an ImageField. An ImageField descriptor is always an attribute (getattr never returns None) and FieldFile always has a .url property. The guard unconditionally reaches `comment.image.url`, which raises `ValueError: The 'image' attribute has no file associated with it.` for every comment saved without an image. Every ListCommentsView and ListRepliesView response containing such a comment will 500.
suggested_fix: Use Django's standard FieldFile truthiness check: `"image_url": comment.image.url if comment.image else None`. FieldFile.__bool__ returns False when name is empty, making this reliable.
verdict_note: Confirmed by reading views.py line 502. The guard `getattr(comment, 'image', None) and hasattr(comment.image, 'url')` is always True for an ImageField — getattr on a model attribute never returns None for a declared field, and FieldFile always has .url. Real 500 on any comment without an image in any list response.

title: ToggleLikeView TOCTOU race: get_or_create outside transaction.atomic
description: Lines 461-472: `Like.objects.get_or_create(...)` runs outside any `transaction.atomic()` block. Two concurrent POST requests from the same user can both observe created=True (SELECT then INSERT race window), causing one INSERT to hit the `unique_together` constraint and raise an unhandled `IntegrityError` (500). Unlike AddCommentView which wraps its write in `transaction.atomic()`, ToggleLikeView has no such protection.
verdict_note: Confirmed. views.py lines 461-472 perform get_or_create + conditional delete with no atomic block. AddCommentView at line 341 uses transaction.atomic() correctly. Like.unique_together is ('author', 'content_type', 'object_id') per models.py line 82, confirming IntegrityError on race.

title: log_new_user sources list has no ordering — returning-user new_service label is non-deterministic
description: Lines 197-202: `EntitySource.objects.filter(entity=profile).values_list('service', flat=True)` has no explicit ordering. Line 214 has the comment `# ordering = ["-updated_at"]` but no `.order_by('-updated_at')` is applied to the query. For a returning user, `sources[0]` is whatever the DB returns first (typically insertion order), not the most recently added source. The admin notification may display the wrong service action label.
suggested_fix:
Add explicit ordering to the query:
sources = list(
    EntitySource.objects.filter(entity=profile)
    .order_by('-updated_at')
    .values_list('service', flat=True)
)
verdict_note: Confirmed. service.py lines 197-202 fetch sources with no order_by clause. The comment on line 214 acknowledges the intended ordering but it is not applied. For a user with multiple sources, sources[0] is non-deterministic.

title: cfg_ callback queries toggle SiteSettings without verifying the caller is the admin
description: _toggle_admin_setting() (lines 336-364) writes to SiteSettings for any callback_query whose data starts with 'cfg_', without checking whether the sender is the site owner or a member of the admin group. _handle_callback() (line 294) dispatches cfg_ callbacks with no identity check. Contrast with _group_command() (line 181) which gates on `chat_id == site.telegram_admin_group_id`. Any Telegram user who sends a cfg_ callback_query — e.g. by copying the inline keyboard message to a private chat or exploiting a Telegram client bug — can silently toggle site-wide notification settings.
suggested_fix:
Add an owner check at the top of _toggle_admin_setting:

def _toggle_admin_setting(self, cq):
    from servermonitor.handlers import is_owner
    tg_id = cq['from']['id']
    cb_id = cq['id']
    if not is_owner(tg_id):
        self.api.answer_callback_query(cb_id, 'Permission denied')
        return
    ...
verdict_note: Confirmed. webhook.py _toggle_admin_setting (line 336) has no caller identity check — no is_owner() call, no admin_group_id comparison. _handle_callback dispatches directly from data.startswith('cfg_') at line 304 with no prior guard. The is_owner helper is already imported and used in _private_command (line 111).

title: Unrestricted ContentType enumeration allows comments/likes on any installed model
description: AddCommentView (line 306), ToggleLikeView (line 452), and ListCommentsView (line 528) accept arbitrary app_label + model_name from the URL/query-string and look up any ContentType installed in Django with no whitelist. An authenticated Telegram user can probe or leave comments on internal models (users/user, contact/contactmessage, core/sitesettings, etc.). The exists() check only confirms a row exists — it discloses object existence for any model. No COMMENTABLE_CONTENT_TYPES allowlist exists anywhere in the codebase.
verdict_note: Confirmed. views.py lines 306 and 452 do ContentType.objects.get(app_label=app_label, model=model_name) with no allowlist check. Grep confirms no COMMENTABLE_CONTENT_TYPES or equivalent whitelist exists in the codebase.

title: Comment image MIME type check relies on spoofable Content-Type header
description: Lines 281-283 check `image.content_type` against an allowlist, but `image.content_type` is the multipart Content-Type header supplied by the client — trivially spoofable. The subsequent `img.verify()` (line 287) detects structurally corrupt files but does not fully decode all image data and is documented as insufficient alone. GIF is in the allowlist but animated GIFs with embedded JavaScript payloads are an XSS vector in older browsers if served from /media/ with a permissive Content-Type.
suggested_fix:
Validate MIME from file bytes, not the header. Use python-magic or Pillow's format attribute after a full open+load:
import magic
image.seek(0)
if magic.from_buffer(image.read(2048), mime=True) not in allowed_mimes:
    return JsonResponse({'error': 'Invalid image format'}, status=400)
image.seek(0)
Also consider removing 'image/gif' from the allowlist if animated GIFs are not needed.
verdict_note: Confirmed. views.py line 282 checks image.content_type which is the client-supplied multipart header. Pillow img.verify() on line 287 is called but only catches corrupt files, not MIME-spoofed non-images. Real bypass path exists.

title: on_reaction_saved fires notify_reaction('added') on emoji-update, not just creation
description: The `on_reaction_saved` signal handler (lines 54-59) has no `if not created: return` guard and always fires `notify_reaction(instance, 'added')`. ToggleCommentReactionView in views.py (lines 418-421) explicitly handles emoji-swap: it updates `reaction.emoji` and calls `reaction.save()` when the user has a different existing reaction. This update-save triggers post_save with `created=False`, so the comment author receives a spurious '+1 <emoji>' DM notification for what was an emoji change. `log_reaction` also logs 'reacted' for this case. Contrast: on_comment_created and on_like_created both have `if not created: return` guards (lines 40, 78).
verdict_note: Confirmed. signals.py lines 54-59 missing 'if not created: return'. views.py lines 418-421 confirm the update path calls reaction.save() with created=False. on_comment_created (line 40) and on_like_created (line 78) both have the guard, making this an inconsistency.

title: Double TelegramEntity SELECT per SSR detail-page render for logged-in users
description: The `core.context_processors.site_settings` context processor (core/context_processors.py line 19) executes `TelegramEntity.objects.get(pk=profile_id)` for every template render. For ProjectDetailView and BlogDetailView, `_interactions_context` (presentation/web/views.py line 68) then calls `get_tg_profile(request)` again — which executes the identical `TelegramEntity.objects.get(pk=profile_id)` a second time. Every logged-in detail-page load issues two identical PK lookups.
suggested_fix: Cache the profile on the request object in the context processor: `request.tg_profile = tg_profile`. Then in _interactions_context, use `getattr(request, 'tg_profile', None)` instead of calling `get_tg_profile(request)`. This eliminates the second DB round-trip with no architectural change.
verdict_note: Confirmed. core/context_processors.py line 19 does TelegramEntity.objects.get(pk=profile_id). presentation/web/views.py line 68 calls get_tg_profile(request) which does the identical TelegramEntity.objects.get(pk=profile_id) lookup a second time.

title: N+1 query: reply_count fallback fires on every comment in ListCommentsView
description: serialize_comment line 508 falls back to `comment.replies.filter(is_approved=True).count()` when the `reply_count` annotation is absent. The sort='top' branch annotates `pcount` (line 544) not `reply_count`, so `getattr(comment, 'reply_count', ...)` always misses the annotation and fires the fallback COUNT query for every comment. The sort='new' branch has no annotation at all. With page_size=10, every list request issues 10 extra SELECT COUNT queries.
suggested_fix:
Rename the annotation from `pcount` to `reply_count` in the sort='top' branch, and add the same annotation to the sort='new' branch using a filtered count to match the serializer:
qs = qs.annotate(
    rcount=Count('reactions', distinct=True),
    reply_count=Count('replies', filter=Q(replies__is_approved=True), distinct=True)
)
This eliminates the fallback path entirely.
verdict_note: Confirmed. views.py line 544 annotates 'pcount' (not 'reply_count'). The serialize_comment fallback at line 508 uses getattr(comment, 'reply_count', ...) which never finds 'pcount', so the .count() fires for every comment on every request.

title: SiteSettingsService.get() called up to 4 times per notification dispatch
description: _admin_enabled (line 301), _send_to_admin_group (line 343), _should_notify (line 386), and _deep_link_button (line 405) each call SiteSettingsService.get() independently. A single notification dispatch (e.g. log_new_comment calls _admin_enabled + _send_to_admin_group + _deep_link_button) hits the cache 3-4 times in one call stack. While each hit is cheap (5-min in-process cache), it is unnecessary churn in daemon threads and makes the call graph harder to reason about.
suggested_fix:
Resolve SiteSettings once at the top of each public method and pass the resolved object to helpers:
site = SiteSettingsService.get()
if not getattr(site, 'admin_notify_comments', True):
    return
...
self._send_to_admin_group(text, ..., site=site)
Add an optional `site` parameter to _deep_link_button and _send_to_admin_group.
verdict_note: Confirmed. service.py: _admin_enabled (line 301), _send_to_admin_group (line 343), _is_site_owner via _should_notify (line 386), _deep_link_button (line 405) all call SiteSettingsService.get() independently.

title: check_ban always runs an UPDATE query even when the user has never been banned
description: check_ban() (called on every comment POST and reaction POST) unconditionally runs an UPDATE to auto-expire mutes (line 56) before the SELECT to fetch an active ban (line 65). On a typical portfolio where no user is ever banned, both queries return zero rows on every single call. The UPDATE acquires a write lock on UserBan rows for a condition that is almost always false.
verdict_note: Confirmed. ban_check.py lines 55-61: the UserBan.objects.filter(...).update(is_active=False) runs unconditionally before the SELECT at line 64. For a user with no ban records ever, this fires a write-path SQL UPDATE on every comment/reaction POST.

title: funstat = {} hardcoded empty makes 30+ lines of conditional branches permanently dead
description: Line 174: `funstat = {}` is hardcoded and never populated. It was the call-site for a removed OSINT/FunStat enrichment API. All downstream `funstat.get(...)` branches (lines 207-252) are permanently dead: fs_name override, username, phone, is_premium, is_verified, is_scam, is_fake, is_bot, is_active. The `is_active` block (lines 248-252) has no `getattr(profile, ...)` fallback — it only reads from funstat, so the 'Faol'/'Nofaol' badge never fires even if TelegramEntity has an is_active field. The code misleads readers into thinking enrichment is conditional when it categorically never runs.
suggested_fix: Delete `funstat = {}` (line 174) and all `funstat.get(...)` guard clauses. Replace every `funstat.get('X') or getattr(profile, 'X', ...)` with just `getattr(profile, 'X', ...)`. The `is_active` block at lines 248-252 should either be dropped or replaced with `getattr(profile, 'is_active', None)` if the field exists on TelegramEntity. This removes ~25 dead lines.
verdict_note: Confirmed. service.py line 174 hardcodes funstat = {}. Lines 207-252 contain 9 conditional branches all gated on funstat.get() which always returns None/False. The is_active badge (lines 248-252) has no profile fallback — it is permanently unreachable. Verified no code ever populates funstat.

title: handle_emoji_callback is a permanent stub — dispatch in webhook.py is always a no-op
description: handle_emoji_callback (lines 62-64 of emoji_admin.py) unconditionally returns False. The caller in webhook.py line 297 (`if handle_emoji_callback(data, callback_query, self.api): return`) therefore never short-circuits. The function, its import in webhook.py line 32, and the dispatch call at line 297 are all dead weight.
suggested_fix: Delete handle_emoji_callback from emoji_admin.py (lines 62-64), remove its import from webhook.py line 32, and remove the dead dispatch guard at webhook.py line 297-298. If emoji callback handling is a planned feature, add a TODO comment at the call-site instead.
verdict_note: Confirmed. emoji_admin.py lines 62-64: `def handle_emoji_callback(...): return False`. webhook.py line 297 imports and calls it unconditionally. The guard `if handle_emoji_callback(...): return` never fires.

title: TelegramBotAPI holds a persistent httpx.Client that is never closed
description: TelegramBotAPI.__init__ (line 26) creates `self._client = httpx.Client(timeout=10.0)` which is stored on the NotificationService singleton for the lifetime of the Django process. There is no __del__, context manager, or explicit close() call. The underlying connection pool accumulates stale TCP connections to api.telegram.org that are never explicitly released — they persist until OS reclamation on process exit.
suggested_fix: Either use a per-call client in _post() — `with httpx.Client(timeout=10.0) as client: resp = client.post(...)` — which is thread-safe and has no shared state, or add a close() method to TelegramBotAPI and call it in a try/finally wrapper in fire_and_forget. The per-call approach is simplest and eliminates the shared-state concern for a low-frequency notification path.
verdict_note: Confirmed. telegram_api.py line 26: self._client = httpx.Client(timeout=10.0) assigned in __init__. No close(), no __del__, no context manager usage anywhere in the file. The client is reused for all _post() calls including multipart sendPhoto (line 124) with a separate timeout override.

title: osint and talabaovozi service labels are dead — those apps no longer exist in this project
description: svc_labels and svc_action_labels (lines 185-193) define lookup keys 'osint' and 'talabaovozi'. The osint app was removed from this repo (CLAUDE.md confirms only blog/contact/core/interactions/ops/portfolio/servermonitor/telegram/users remain). 'talabaovozi' is a codename for an entirely different project (EduStats). No code path in jaysonkhan_v2 can create EntitySource records with these service values. The labels are permanently unreachable dead strings that mislead readers about active services.
suggested_fix: Remove the 'osint' and 'talabaovozi' entries from both svc_labels and svc_action_labels. The only active service key for this portfolio-only project is 'site'. If any prod DB still has legacy EntitySource rows with service='osint', keep 'osint' but add a comment: `# legacy-display only — osint app removed`.
verdict_note: Confirmed. service.py lines 185-193 define 'osint' and 'talabaovozi' label keys. CLAUDE.md lists installed apps: no osint, no talabaovozi. No EntitySource creation code in jaysonkhan_v2 uses these service values.

title: edit_message_text is defined but has zero call-sites in the entire backend
description: TelegramBotAPI.edit_message_text (lines 161-178) is a public method with no call-sites anywhere in the backend. Grep confirms the only occurrence is the definition. Webhook handlers exclusively use edit_message_reply_markup for in-place keyboard updates, never text edits. The method was likely pre-built for a bot flow removed with the osint/botproxy apps.
suggested_fix: Delete the method (lines 161-178). It can be re-added when an actual use-case arises.
verdict_note: Confirmed. Grep of entire backend for 'edit_message_text' returns exactly one result: the definition at telegram_api.py line 161. No callers exist anywhere in the codebase.

title: MONITORED_SERVICES is list[dict] but handlers.py treats it as list[str] — runtime crashes in /services, /logs, and svc_restart_* callbacks
description: metrics.py defines MONITORED_SERVICES as list[dict] (keys: unit, group, display, critical), but handlers.py was never updated to match. Four call sites break at runtime: (1) Line 98: `collect_service_status(s)` passes the whole dict as service_name — _systemctl receives a dict object; (2) Line 163: `service not in MONITORED_SERVICES` compares a str to a list[dict] — always False, so the allowlist is completely bypassed; (3) Line 167: `', '.join(MONITORED_SERVICES)` raises TypeError because join requires str items; (4) Line 235 (svc_refresh) repeats the dict-passthrough to collect_service_status, and line 250 (svc_restart_*) repeats the str-in-list[dict] check — always True, so no restart is ever allowed. The management command service_health_check.py is already correct (uses cfg['unit'] etc.). collect_full_snapshot() in metrics.py also already unpacks correctly.
suggested_fix: Add a module-level set at the top of handlers.py: `_UNIT_NAMES = frozenset(cfg['unit'] for cfg in MONITORED_SERVICES)`. Fix lines 98 and 235: `collect_service_status(s['unit'], group=s['group'], display=s['display'], critical=s.get('critical', True)) for s in MONITORED_SERVICES`. Fix line 163: `if service not in _UNIT_NAMES:`. Fix line 167: `', '.join(_UNIT_NAMES)`. Fix line 250: `if service_name not in _UNIT_NAMES:`.
verdict_note: Verified: MONITORED_SERVICES at metrics.py line 274 is explicitly typed list[dict]. All four broken call sites in handlers.py confirmed by direct code reading. /services command and svc_refresh/svc_restart_ callbacks are all broken at runtime.

title: MemoryCurrent=18446744073709551615 (systemd N/A sentinel) stored as ~17592186044416 MB
description: Line 238: `if val.isdigit()` passes for systemd's not-available sentinel 2^64-1 (18446744073709551615), which systemd returns when memory accounting is disabled for a unit. The code then stores approximately 17.6 petabytes as memory_mb. This renders as a nonsensical number in Telegram messages and could mislead the tariff advisor.
suggested_fix: Add an upper-bound guard after the isdigit check: `mem_bytes = int(val); if 0 < mem_bytes < (1 << 62): mem_mb = round(mem_bytes / (1024 * 1024), 1)`. This excludes the 2^64-1 sentinel and any near-max uint64 values that are also not real memory readings.
verdict_note: Verified: lines 237-239 use val.isdigit() with no upper-bound check. The sentinel value passes isdigit() and is processed without guard.

title: format_cron_failure_alert uses UTC .strftime on tz-aware datetimes — displayed times are UTC not local
description: Line 341: `f['started_at'].strftime('%H:%M:%S')` and line 353 both call strftime directly on datetimes from .values() queries over CronRun.started_at. With USE_TZ=True (production default) these are UTC-aware datetime objects. The operator receives e.g. '03:15:00' when local server time is '06:15:00 +03:00'.
suggested_fix: Use `django.utils.timezone.localtime(f['started_at']).strftime(...)` for both the failures loop (line 341) and the overdue loop (line 353).
verdict_note: Verified: lines 341 and 353 call .strftime() directly on datetime values coming from ORM .values() queries. No localtime() conversion present.

title: pg_dump backup written to world-readable /tmp — dump never sent to Telegram and never cleaned up
description: Line 198: pg_dump writes to /tmp/jaysonkhan_backup.dump with the process's default umask (typically 0644 on Linux). /tmp is world-readable (mode 1777), so any local OS user can read the full database dump. The path is deterministic, enabling a local race during the pg_dump write. The dump is never deleted — successive runs silently overwrite it. Additionally, line 209-214 confirms only a text message with the local path is sent to Telegram; the file is never transmitted. The send_document method does exist in TelegramBotAPI (confirmed absent from this code path).
suggested_fix: Write to a directory owned only by the deploy user (e.g. /var/www/jaysonkhan/backups/, mode 0700), or use tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='wb', suffix='.dump', delete=False) with os.chmod(path, 0o600) immediately after creation. After a successful pg_dump, send the file using api.send_document() (method exists in TelegramBotAPI) and then delete the temp file with os.unlink().
verdict_note: Verified: line 198 hardcodes /tmp path. Lines 209-214 confirm only a text success message is sent — no send_document call. No os.unlink or cleanup present. TelegramBotAPI.send_document not present (no send_document in telegram_api.py).

title: svc_refresh callback discards freshly computed message text — stale status remains visible
description: The svc_refresh callback (lines 233-246) re-collects service status and computes fresh text via `text = format_services(services)` at line 236, then rebuilds the keyboard — but calls only `api.edit_message_reply_markup(...)` at line 240, discarding the freshly computed `text`. The message body stays unchanged showing stale service statuses. `TelegramBotAPI.edit_message_text` exists (confirmed at telegram_api.py line 161) and accepts both text and reply_markup.
suggested_fix: Replace the `api.edit_message_reply_markup(...)` call with `api.edit_message_text(chat_id=msg['chat']['id'], message_id=msg['message_id'], text=text, reply_markup=keyboard)` so both the status text and inline keyboard are updated atomically.
verdict_note: Verified: line 236 assigns text but it is not used. Line 240-244 calls edit_message_reply_markup only. edit_message_text exists in TelegramBotAPI at line 161 and accepts reply_markup as an optional parameter.

title: N+1 DB queries in cron_health_check overdue loop — one CronRun query per ManagedCron row
description: Lines 84-99: the loop fetches all enabled ManagedCron rows then issues a separate CronRun.objects.filter(command=...).order_by('-started_at').first() per managed cron — N+1 queries. The same N+1 pattern is duplicated in server_health_report._cron_summary_24h() at lines 70-74.
suggested_fix: Pre-fetch all last-run timestamps in one annotated query before the loop: `from django.db.models import Max; last_runs = dict(CronRun.objects.filter(command__in=[mc.command for mc in managed_crons]).values('command').annotate(last=Max('started_at')).values_list('command', 'last'))`. Then replace the per-mc inner query with `last_runs.get(mc.command)`. Apply the same fix in _cron_summary_24h().
verdict_note: Verified: cron_health_check.py line 88-92 does a .first() query inside the per-ManagedCron loop. server_health_report.py lines 71-73 repeat the same pattern independently.

title: N+1 DB queries in service_health_check — one ServiceCheckResult lookup per service unit
description: Lines 76-80: the per-service loop issues a separate ServiceCheckResult.objects.filter(service_unit=unit).order_by('-checked_at').only('is_active').first() for each of the 11 monitored services — 11 separate DB round-trips on every 5-minute cron tick.
suggested_fix: Pre-fetch all 11 latest rows before the loop. A clean approach: `from django.db.models import Max; latest = {r['service_unit']: r['last'] for r in ServiceCheckResult.objects.filter(service_unit__in=units).values('service_unit').annotate(last=Max('checked_at'))}`. Then join to fetch the is_active values for those specific timestamps, or use a DISTINCT ON raw query.
verdict_note: Verified: service_health_check.py lines 76-80 perform a .first() query inside the loop over MONITORED_SERVICES (11 services).

title: server_health_report overdue check uses flat 24h window ignoring each cron's actual schedule
description: In _cron_summary_24h() at line 74, a managed cron is flagged overdue if `(now - last_seen) > REPORT_WINDOW` where REPORT_WINDOW = timedelta(hours=24). A 5-minute cron that last ran 2 hours ago will not be flagged here (correct), but a 6-hourly cron that ran 7 hours ago will be flagged even though it is only one window behind schedule. More critically, cron_health_check.py correctly uses `interval * OVERDUE_MULTIPLIER` (2x) per schedule — this file ignores schedule entirely, producing an unreliable overdue list in the daily report.
suggested_fix: Import _expected_interval from cron_health_check (or move it to a shared utility in servermonitor/utils.py). Replace line 74: `if not last_seen or (now - last_seen) > REPORT_WINDOW:` with `interval = _expected_interval(mc.schedule); threshold = (interval * 2) if interval else REPORT_WINDOW; if not last_seen or (now - last_seen) > threshold:`.
verdict_note: Verified: server_health_report.py line 74 uses REPORT_WINDOW (24h) flat. cron_health_check.py line 94 uses `interval * OVERDUE_MULTIPLIER`. The two implementations are inconsistent. _expected_interval is not imported in server_health_report.py.

title: CLAUDE.md documents removed botproxy and osint apps as present — stale references mislead contributors
description: CLAUDE.md lines 44 and 47 list apps/botproxy/ and apps/osint/ in the folder tree, and line 166 references apps/botproxy/client.py. Neither app exists in the repo (confirmed: `ls backend/apps/` shows blog, contact, core, interactions, ops, portfolio, servermonitor, telegram, users — no botproxy or osint). Lines 193-195 reference BOT_API_BASE_URL, BOT_API_SECRET_KEY, and BOT_API_TIMEOUT env vars whose only consumer was the removed botproxy client.
suggested_fix: Remove the botproxy/ and osint/ lines from the folder tree. Delete note 15 (Bot API auth — botproxy/client.py reference). Remove BOT_API_BASE_URL, BOT_API_SECRET_KEY, and BOT_API_TIMEOUT from the Environment variables table if no other module uses them.
verdict_note: Verified: `ls backend/apps/` confirms neither botproxy nor osint directory exists. CLAUDE.md still lists both in the tree and references client.py. This matches the brief's note that both were removed 2026-05-31.

title: Author email exposed via public post detail endpoint
description: PostViewSet uses permission_classes = [permissions.AllowAny] and the detail/retrieve action returns PostSerializer, which nests UserSerializer. UserSerializer.Meta.fields explicitly includes 'email' (line 13). Any anonymous visitor hitting GET /api/posts/{id}/ receives the post author's email address in the JSON response. Since the site has a single owner-author, this leaks the owner's personal email to scrapers and the public internet.
verdict_note: Confirmed: PostViewSet.permission_classes = [AllowAny] (views.py:87), get_serializer_class returns PostSerializer for detail action (views.py:92), PostSerializer.author = UserSerializer(read_only=True) (serializers.py:81), UserSerializer.Meta.fields includes 'email' (serializers.py:13). Direct information disclosure.

title: SiteSettingsSerializer raises KeyError when instantiated without request context
description: All five get_*_url methods in SiteSettingsSerializer call self.context['request'] with a hard bracket lookup (lines 142, 145, 148, 151, 154). Instantiating the serializer without a request context (e.g. in management commands, tests, or any shell inspection) raises KeyError. The current sole caller (SiteSettingsView.get) always passes context={'request': request}, so no production 500 today. However the inconsistency with the safer self.context.get('request') pattern used by ProjectListSerializer (line 51) and PostListSerializer (line 103) is a latent fragility.
verdict_note: Confirmed experimentally: instantiating SiteSettingsSerializer(obj) without context raises KeyError: 'request'. The fix is safe because _url already guards on not field_value, so adding not request simply returns None for context-less calls — matching the empty-field behaviour.

title: Contact API create bypasses honeypot and IP rate-limit checks
description: ContactMessageViewSet.create (AllowAny, /api/contact/) relies solely on DRF's global AnonRateThrottle (30/min). The SSR form view (presentation/web/views.py:333,337) calls the existing is_honeypot_filled() and is_rate_limited() helpers from apps/contact/spam_protection.py, but the API path never does. A bot posting directly to /api/contact/ bypasses the honeypot entirely and can send 30 spam messages per minute, each triggering an email notification.
verdict_note: Confirmed: spam_protection.py contains is_honeypot_filled and is_rate_limited; web views.py uses them at lines 333/337; ContactMessageViewSet.create has no call to either. The AnonRateThrottle at 30/min is the only gate.

title: X-Forwarded-For IP spoofing bypasses contact rate limiter
description: _get_client_ip() takes the leftmost value of X-Forwarded-For (line 55: xff.split(',')[0].strip()). Nginx is configured with proxy_add_x_forwarded_for, which appends the real client IP to any attacker-supplied XFF header before passing it upstream. The application then reads the first (attacker-controlled) value as the cache key, making is_rate_limited() trivially bypassable by sending X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4. DRF's AnonRateThrottle has the same exposure since NUM_PROXIES is not set in REST_FRAMEWORK settings.
verdict_note: Confirmed: nginx.conf line 227 uses proxy_add_x_forwarded_for which prepends client-supplied XFF; spam_protection.py:55 takes xff.split(',')[0] (leftmost = client-controlled). REST_FRAMEWORK settings have no NUM_PROXIES key.

title: SkillViewSet.queryset references removed fields 'level' and 'icon' — FieldDoesNotExist on every request
description: Migration 0015 (remove_skill_icon_remove_skill_level_and_more) dropped icon, level, and show_in_hero from the Skill model. SkillViewSet.queryset still calls Skill.objects.only('id', 'name', 'level', 'icon', 'category', 'order'). Verified experimentally: this raises FieldDoesNotExist: Skill has no field named 'icon' on every queryset evaluation. The endpoint is IsAdminUser-gated so unauthenticated users cannot trigger it, but any admin hitting GET /api/skills/ gets a 500.
suggested_fix:
Update the only() call to match the current Skill model:

queryset = Skill.objects.only('id', 'name', 'category', 'order').all()

Also update SkillSerializer to enumerate fields explicitly instead of fields = '__all__' to make future field removals visible at the serializer level:

class SkillSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    category_display = serializers.CharField(source='get_category_display', read_only=True)
    class Meta:
        model = Skill
        fields = ('id', 'name', 'category', 'category_display', 'order')
verdict_note: Confirmed experimentally with venv/bin/python: Skill.objects.only('id', 'name', 'level', 'icon', 'category', 'order') raises FieldDoesNotExist: Skill has no field named 'icon'. Migration 0015 confirmed removal. Skill.objects.only('id', 'name', 'category', 'order') works correctly.

title: PostListSerializer.reading_time triggers a deferred-field DB hit per row
description: PostViewSet.get_queryset() calls .defer('content_rich') on the list action to avoid loading the large HTML field. PostListSerializer.Meta.fields includes reading_time (line 99), which is a @property on Post (blog/models.py:55-58) that calls strip_tags(self.content_rich or ''). Accessing content_rich on a deferred row triggers a separate SQL SELECT per object. Verified experimentally: accessing reading_time on a deferred Post fires 1 extra query fetching content_rich_xo (the translated field). With 10 posts per page, this is 10 extra round-trips, negating the defer() optimization.
suggested_fix:
Option A (surgical): remove 'reading_time' from PostListSerializer.Meta.fields. Post list cards typically show title/excerpt/date — reading time is only needed on the detail page where content_rich is not deferred.

Option B (preserve feature): add a stored integer field reading_time_minutes populated on save() so it can be included in queries without touching content_rich.
verdict_note: Confirmed experimentally: Post.objects.filter(is_published=True).defer('content_rich') + accessing p.reading_time fires 1 additional SQL query selecting blog_post.content_rich_xo. The 10-row-per-page N+1 is real.

title: ShareToChannelView blocks Gunicorn sync worker with synchronous Telegram HTTP (60s timeout)
description: ShareToChannelView.post() calls ChannelShareService.share_post/share_project() synchronously inline in the request path. TelegramBotAPI (interactions/notifications/telegram_api.py:124) uses a 60-second timeout for multipart photo uploads. The project runs 3 Gunicorn sync workers (per CLAUDE.md). A single admin share that triggers the multipart path holds a worker for up to 60s. A second concurrent share saturates the pool to 2/3 capacity. This violates the CLAUDE.md invariant: 'Parallel bot calls use ThreadPoolExecutor, NOT asyncio.gather'.
verdict_note: Confirmed: channel_share.py calls self.api.send_photo() and send_message() synchronously; telegram_api.py:124 has explicit timeout=60.0 for multipart. No ThreadPoolExecutor or thread offload in ShareToChannelView. CLAUDE.md explicitly mandates ThreadPoolExecutor for bot API calls.

title: User.USERNAME_FIELD not overridden — /api/token/ accepts username not email
description: The custom User model docstring states 'email is the unique identifier for authentication instead of usernames', and email is declared unique=True. However USERNAME_FIELD is never set to 'email'. Verified: User.USERNAME_FIELD = 'username' (the AbstractUser default). SimpleJWT's TokenObtainPairView at /api/token/ derives its login field from USERNAME_FIELD, so the JWT endpoint requires a username payload, not email — the opposite of what the model contract promises. Any admin tooling or test code expecting email + password login will receive 401.
suggested_fix:
In apps/users/models.py, add:

USERNAME_FIELD = 'email'
REQUIRED_FIELDS = []  # remove email from extras since it's now the primary field

Also update __str__ to return self.email (currently returns self.username). No custom authentication backend is needed — Django's default ModelBackend respects USERNAME_FIELD. Verify existing admin user still works (may need to migrate or reset).
verdict_note: Confirmed: User.USERNAME_FIELD resolves to 'username' (AbstractUser default), model docstring claims email-based auth. config/urls.py:41 registers TokenObtainPairView at /api/token/ which uses USERNAME_FIELD.

title: ContactMessageSerializer omits is_read — admin cannot see or update read status via API
description: ContactMessage.is_read (BooleanField, default=False) exists on the model and has a DB index (contact_date_read). ContactMessageSerializer.Meta.fields is an explicit tuple that omits is_read. ContactMessageViewSet is a full ModelViewSet — admin-authenticated GETs (list, retrieve) cannot see read status, and PATCH/PUT cannot set is_read=True. The feature is half-implemented: the model and index are there but the API wire format hides them.
verdict_note: Confirmed: ContactMessage model has is_read = BooleanField(default=False) with DB index. Serializer field tuple at line 114 lists only (id, name, email, subject, message, created_at) — is_read absent. ContactMessageViewSet is ModelViewSet with no override for read/update actions.

title: Misleading 'Inherits IsAdminUser' comment inside AllowAny ProjectViewSet
description: ProjectViewSet has permission_classes = [permissions.AllowAny] at class level (line 34), making all project endpoints public. However line 61 has the comment '# Inherits IsAdminUser from REST_FRAMEWORK default', which is factually wrong for this class. The same comment is correctly placed on IsAdminUser-gated viewsets (SkillViewSet:29, ExperienceViewSet:68, etc.), but its appearance inside ProjectViewSet inverts the actual permission posture for any developer auditing access control.
suggested_fix:
Replace the comment at line 61 with one that accurately reflects the intent:

# Public: AllowAny set at class level (portfolio projects are intentionally public)

Or remove it entirely since the explicit permission_classes = [permissions.AllowAny] on line 34 is self-documenting.
verdict_note: Confirmed: views.py:34 has permission_classes = [permissions.AllowAny]; views.py:61 has '# Inherits IsAdminUser from REST_FRAMEWORK default' — directly contradicting the class-level override.

title: Stale osint deep-link parameters in TgAppRouterView docstring
description: TgAppRouterView docstring (lines 384-385) lists 'osint-p-{id}' and 'osint-e-{id}' as supported startapp parameters. The osint app was removed from this project (per CLAUDE.md: 'osint removed 2026-05-31'). _resolve_target() has no handler for either prefix — they fall through silently to the home page redirect. The docstring is a stale contract that misleads future deep-link work.
suggested_fix: Delete lines 384-385 from the docstring. The live parameter list is already documented by the remaining entries: c-{id}, post-{slug}, proj-{slug}, and home.
verdict_note: Confirmed: presentation/web/views.py:384-385 lists osint-p and osint-e parameters; CLAUDE.md confirms osint app removed 2026-05-31; _resolve_target has no osint handler (confirmed by grep showing only c-, post-, proj- prefixes are handled).

title: Public GET /api/posts/{id}/ leaks admin user email via nested UserSerializer
description: PostViewSet sets permission_classes = [AllowAny] (api/views.py:87). Its detail action returns PostSerializer, which nests UserSerializer with fields = ('id', 'username', 'email', 'bio', 'profile_picture'). Every unauthenticated GET /api/posts/<id>/ therefore includes the site owner's email address. The list action uses PostListSerializer (no author field) so it is unaffected; only the detail action leaks.
suggested_fix: Create a PublicAuthorSerializer with only safe fields (e.g. 'id', 'username', 'bio', 'profile_picture') and use it in PostSerializer instead of UserSerializer. Do not expose 'email' in any AllowAny-accessible serializer.
verdict_note: Confirmed. PostViewSet at api/views.py:87 sets AllowAny; get_serializer_class returns PostSerializer for detail action; PostSerializer at serializers.py:81 nests UserSerializer which explicitly includes 'email'.

title: Stored XSS via innerHTML in team.html dossier modal
description: The openMember() function builds the dossier modal HTML by string-concatenating m.name, m.role, m.bio, m.quote, m.photo, m.skills[], and social link URLs directly into body.innerHTML without escaping. json_script ensures safe JSON encoding at the Django boundary, but the JS side treats the resulting strings as trusted HTML. An admin-edited bio or name containing will execute in every visitor's browser when they open the dossier.
suggested_fix: Replace innerHTML string concatenation in openMember() with DOM API calls (createElement, textContent, setAttribute) so strings are never treated as markup. For photo URL and social links, validate the URL scheme (allow only https:// or relative paths) before setting as src/href.
verdict_note: Confirmed. team.html:194-214 shows direct string concatenation of m.name, m.role, m.bio, m.quote etc. into body.innerHTML. No escaping applied on the JS side.

title: TelegramAuthView (GET, @csrf_exempt) has no same-origin guard — enables cross-site session hijack
description: TelegramAuthView is @csrf_exempt and handles GET with no _is_same_origin() check (interactions/views.py:88-117). It writes request.session[SESSION_KEY] = entity.pk after HMAC-verifying Telegram data. An attacker can craft a URL with a valid Telegram auth payload issued for their own account and trick a victim into visiting it, binding the victim's browser session to the attacker's Telegram identity. Unlike AddCommentView, ToggleLikeView, and ToggleCommentReactionView which gate on _is_same_origin(), TelegramAuthView has no such guard. TelegramLoginView and TelegramWebAppLoginView (both @csrf_exempt POST) also lack the guard.
suggested_fix: Add _is_same_origin(request) check at the top of TelegramAuthView.get() and return JsonResponse({'error': 'Forbidden'}, status=403) on failure, matching the pattern already used in AddCommentView at line 237. Apply the same guard to TelegramLoginView.post() and TelegramWebAppLoginView.post().
verdict_note: Confirmed. TelegramAuthView at line 96 does not call _is_same_origin(); it verifies the Telegram HMAC but that only authenticates the identity in the payload — not that the request originated from the site owner's browser. The session-fixation vector is real.

title: IP rate-limit on contact form and visitor tracking bypassed by spoofed X-Forwarded-For
description: spam_protection._get_client_ip() takes xff.split(',')[0].strip() (line 53-55), which is the attacker-controlled first element of X-Forwarded-For. Nginx passes X-Forwarded-For: $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for (confirmed in security/nginx/jaysonkhan.conf:227), appending $remote_addr to whatever the client sends. An attacker can rotate fake IPs to bypass the 3-submission/10-min window entirely. The same pattern exists in HomeView._get_client_ip() (views.py:134-139), which affects visitor-count inflation.
suggested_fix: Use HTTP_X_REAL_IP which Nginx sets from $remote_addr (the true client, unjammable): ip = request.META.get('HTTP_X_REAL_IP') or request.META.get('REMOTE_ADDR', '0.0.0.0'). Apply the same fix to HomeView._get_client_ip(). X-Real-IP is set by Nginx, not forwarded from the client.
verdict_note: Confirmed. Nginx config at jaysonkhan.conf:226-227 sets both X-Real-IP $remote_addr and X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for. The code reads X-Forwarded-For and takes the first element, which is client-controlled. X-Real-IP is available and safe.

title: HomeView: malformed jk_visitor cookie creates a new PageView on every request, never healing the cookie
description: When jk_visitor cookie contains a non-UUID value, the except ValueError branch (line 153) generates uid = uuid.uuid4(). The code then falls into the 'if visitor_id:' branch which may call PageView.objects.create() for the new UUID (since it won't exist in the DB). Critically, no response.set_cookie() is called in this branch — the malformed cookie remains. On every subsequent request, the same malformed value is sent, the same new UUID is generated, and if the DB check fails, a new PageView is created each time, inflating the visitor count indefinitely.
suggested_fix: When the ValueError branch is taken, treat it the same as no cookie (fall through to Case 3) by setting response.set_cookie() with the new uid, ensuring the browser receives a valid UUID on the very next response. Alternatively, call response.delete_cookie(self.VISITOR_COOKIE) to clear the malformed value so the next request lands in the clean else branch.
verdict_note: Confirmed by reading views.py:147-181. The except ValueError at line 152-153 creates a fresh uid but never calls set_cookie; the malformed cookie persists unchanged. The PageView.objects.create() at line 155 can fire on every request for this visitor.

title: ContactView.post: form input not repopulated on validation error — user loses all entered data
description: On required-fields failure (line 350-352) and on rate-limit (line 341-342), render_to_response(self.get_context_data()) returns a fresh empty context with no POST data. The contact template renders bare input fields with no value= attributes bound to request.POST. All user-typed content (name, email, subject, message) is silently discarded. Users must retype long messages after validation errors.
suggested_fix: Pass POST data into context: return self.render_to_response(self.get_context_data(form_data=request.POST)). In the template, add value="{{ form_data.name|default:'' }}" etc. to each input. Alternatively, use a Django Form class and pass it as context['form'].
verdict_note: Confirmed. views.py:342 and 352 both call self.get_context_data() with no POST data argument; get_context_data() (line 359-361) adds nothing from request.POST to context.

title: SiteSettings.load() bypasses 5-minute cache in three view call sites
description: Three call sites call SiteSettings.load() (which issues a get_or_create DB query every time) instead of SiteSettingsService.get() (5-min cache, post_save invalidation). Call sites: custom_404_view (line 34) — hit on every 404 response; custom_500_view (line 46) — hit on every 500 response; _apps_visible() (line 86) — hit on every ProjectListView and ProjectDetailView request via AppsGuardMixin.dispatch. SiteSettingsService.get() already exists in core/services.py and is used correctly by the context processor.
suggested_fix: Add 'from core.services import SiteSettingsService' to views.py and replace SiteSettings.load() at lines 34, 46, and 86 with SiteSettingsService.get(). Remove SiteSettings from the imports at line 8 if no other direct model reference remains.
verdict_note: Confirmed. views.py imports SiteSettings at line 8 and calls .load() at lines 34, 46, 86. SiteSettingsService with 5-min cache exists at apps/core/services.py:28 and is correctly used by the context processor but not by these three view call sites.

title: SkillSerializer, ExperienceSerializer, CategorySerializer, TagSerializer use fields='__all__' under IsAdminUser
description: SkillSerializer (line 20), ExperienceSerializer (line 62), CategorySerializer (line 70), and TagSerializer (line 74) all use fields='__all__'. These viewsets are currently IsAdminUser. However ProjectViewSet and PostViewSet demonstrate that permission_classes can be overridden to AllowAny. If the same is done for any of these viewsets, the full model schema including any future internal fields would be immediately public. Defence-in-depth gap.
suggested_fix: Declare explicit field lists in each serializer, keeping only fields with a legitimate admin use. This makes the exposure surface predictable regardless of future permission changes.
verdict_note: Confirmed. serializers.py shows SkillSerializer:fields='__all__', ExperienceSerializer:fields='__all__', CategorySerializer:fields='__all__', TagSerializer:fields='__all__'. api/views.py confirms IsAdminUser is inherited (not set explicitly) — same pattern that led to PostViewSet's AllowAny override.

title: Double queryset evaluation in PortfolioService.get_homepage_data()
description: featured = self.repository.get_featured_projects() returns a lazy QuerySet. At line 95, 'if not featured' calls bool() on the queryset, which triggers a SELECT. The template then iterates 'featured_projects' (the same queryset object at line 93), which triggers a second SELECT. Two identical DB queries on every homepage load when featured projects exist.
suggested_fix: Evaluate once with list(): featured = list(self.repository.get_featured_projects()). The bool check on a list is free, and the template iteration reuses the already-fetched list. prefetch_related is preserved because list() fully evaluates the queryset including prefetches.
verdict_note: Confirmed. portfolio/services.py:91-98 shows featured = self.repository.get_featured_projects() (lazy queryset), then 'if not featured' (first evaluation), and 'featured_projects': featured in the returned dict (second evaluation by template). No list() or cache wrapping present.

title: HomeView Case 2: double DB query for same IP (exists() + first())
description: In the 'no cookie, known IP' branch (Case 2), line 157 calls PageView.objects.filter(ip_address=ip).exists() and then line 160 calls PageView.objects.filter(ip_address=ip).first() — two separate DB round-trips against the same indexed column for one cookie-setting operation.
suggested_fix: Replace the exists()+first() pair with a single .first() call: existing = PageView.objects.filter(ip_address=ip).first(); if existing: response.set_cookie(..., str(existing.visitor_id), ...)
verdict_note: Confirmed. views.py:157 and 160 are two separate QuerySet.filter(ip_address=ip) calls in sequence — exists() then first().

title: BlogRepository._PUBLISHED_BASE is dead code — never used, misleads readers
description: Lines 7-12 define a class-level QuerySet chain _PUBLISHED_BASE on BlogRepository. No static method in the class references it; all methods construct their own base querysets. The dead attribute could mislead future readers into calling cls._PUBLISHED_BASE.defer('content_rich') expecting it to behave as a base — but that would share a single QuerySet object across callers (QuerySet result-caching pitfall). It is also built at class-definition time, before the Django app registry is ready in tests.
suggested_fix: Remove the _PUBLISHED_BASE class attribute at lines 7-12 entirely. Each method already constructs its own correct queryset.
verdict_note: Confirmed. blog/services.py:7-12 defines _PUBLISHED_BASE. Searched all methods in BlogRepository (get_published_posts, get_post_by_slug, search_posts, get_related_posts, get_categories) — none reference _PUBLISHED_BASE. It is dead code.

title: PortfolioRepository.get_all_experience() calls bare select_related() with no arguments
description: Experience.objects.select_related().order_by('-start_date') calls select_related() with no arguments. The Experience model has no ForeignKey fields, so this is a no-op today. However, select_related() with no args tells Django to follow ALL FK/OneToOneField relationships recursively — if a FK is added later, this silently becomes an unbounded JOIN. The pattern also misleads readers into thinking a specific relation is being optimized.
suggested_fix: Since Experience has no FK fields, simply remove the select_related() call: Experience.objects.order_by('-start_date'). If a FK is added in future, name it explicitly.
verdict_note: Confirmed. portfolio/services.py:67 shows select_related() with no args. portfolio/models.py:124-142 confirms Experience has no ForeignKey or OneToOneField fields.

title: Font Awesome icons in channel_share.html but FA is not loaded — spinner and error indicators invisible
description: channel_share.html uses fa-solid fa-lock (line 11), fa-solid fa-circle-notch fa-spin (line 57), and fa-solid fa-triangle-exclamation (lines 91, 105). The partial is admin-only, but the loading spinner and error indicator are non-functional for the admin on every share attempt. The static lock icon is also invisible.

title: TgAppRouterView docstring advertises removed osint deep links
description: The TgAppRouterView docstring at lines 384-385 lists 'osint-p-{id} → OSINT foydalanuvchi profili' and 'osint-e-{id} → OSINT entity (kanal/guruh) profili'. The osint app was removed from the project (apps/ directory has no osint app). The _resolve_target method has no handler for these prefixes — they silently fall through to home. title: updateReactionDOM leaves active state unset for previously-active reactions after a toggle
description: updateReactionDOM sets active class only for the currentEmoji (line 1004). The else-if branch at line 1006 for other emojis is empty with an acknowledged TODO comment: 'Full state should come from backend, but optimistic works fine for now.' The backend's reactions dict contains all emojis but not which ones the current user has reacted to. Any emoji the user previously reacted to (besides currentEmoji) will lose its active class after a toggle, giving incorrect visual feedback.
