title: SkillViewSet.queryset references removed fields 'level' and 'icon'
description: Migration 0015 removed the `icon`, `level`, and `show_in_hero` columns from the Skill table. SkillViewSet.queryset still calls `.only('id', 'name', 'level', 'icon', 'category', 'order')`. Django raises FieldError at query time when this queryset is evaluated, crashing any request to /api/skills/ with a 500. The current Skill model only has `name`, `category`, and `order` (plus `id`).
suggested_fix: Change the queryset to: Skill.objects.only('id', 'name', 'category', 'order').all() — matching what PortfolioRepository.get_all_skills() already does correctly.
verdict_note: Verified: migration 0015 removes icon/level/show_in_hero (confirmed in migration file). Skill model in models.py has no icon or level fields. SkillViewSet line 26 still names them. Real crash on any admin GET to /api/skills/.

title: AdminIPRestrictionMiddleware IP-spoofing bypass via X-Forwarded-For
description: AdminIPRestrictionMiddleware._get_ip() reads xff.split(',')[0].strip() — the leftmost (attacker-controlled) entry in X-Forwarded-For. Nginx uses 'proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for' (nginx config lines 227/238/252/263/274), which appends the real client IP to whatever the client already supplied. An attacker sends 'X-Forwarded-For: <whitelisted-ip>' and Django sees '<whitelisted-ip>, <nginx-remote-addr>'; the middleware reads the first entry and grants admin panel access. The same XFF-first-entry bug exists in spam_protection._get_client_ip() (line 55), making the contact rate-limit trivially bypassable.
suggested_fix: Read the rightmost entry instead: xff.split(',')[-1].strip(). This is the IP appended by Nginx and is not attacker-controllable. Apply to both AdminIPRestrictionMiddleware._get_ip() (line 141) and RequestSanitizationMiddleware._get_ip() (line 112) and spam_protection._get_client_ip() (line 55). Alternatively, change the Nginx directive to 'proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr' (overwrites instead of appending), which makes reading [0] safe.
verdict_note: Verified: security_middleware.py line 141 uses split(',')[0]. nginx config confirmed at lines 227/238/252/263/274 uses $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for (append, not overwrite). Both _get_ip() methods (lines 112 and 141) have the same vulnerability.

title: Admin email exposed to unauthenticated callers via public GET /api/posts/<id>/
description: PostSerializer nests UserSerializer (line 81) which includes the 'email' field. PostViewSet has permission_classes = [permissions.AllowAny] and returns PostSerializer for the retrieve action (not PostListSerializer). Any unauthenticated HTTP client calling GET /api/posts/<id>/ receives the author's email address. Since this is a personal portfolio with a single admin, this is the site owner's private email.
suggested_fix: Create a PublicAuthorSerializer that omits 'email' and any internal fields, exposing only display-safe fields (e.g. first_name, last_name or a display_name, bio, profile_picture). Use it in PostSerializer. The full UserSerializer with email is appropriate only for admin-gated views.
verdict_note: Verified: serializers.py line 81 PostSerializer nests UserSerializer with email. views.py line 87 PostViewSet has AllowAny. retrieve action returns PostSerializer (line 92). Confirmed real PII exposure.

title: POST /api/contact/ bypasses honeypot and rate-limit entirely
description: ContactMessageViewSet.create has AllowAny with no spam checks. The honeypot (is_honeypot_filled) and rate-limit (is_rate_limited) from contact/spam_protection.py are only wired into the SSR ContactView (presentation/web/views.py lines 333-337). The DRF endpoint at POST /api/contact/ is a completely separate code path. The honeypot check also reads from request.POST which is empty for JSON API calls, so it is structurally inapplicable. DRF's default AnonRateThrottle is the only guard, which is far weaker (30/min vs 3/10min).
suggested_fix: Override perform_create in ContactMessageViewSet to call is_rate_limited(request). The rate-limit check only needs the request IP so it works for both form and JSON submissions. The honeypot check is inherently form-only; document this. Alternatively add a custom DRF throttle class that enforces the 3/600s limit on this endpoint.
verdict_note: Verified: views.py lines 110-121 ContactMessageViewSet.create has AllowAny with no spam checks. SSR ContactView at lines 333-337 has the checks. spam_protection.py line 23 reads request.POST.get('website') — inapplicable to JSON API.

title: Project.save() sanitizes only the active-locale description_rich; other locale columns bypass bleach
description: With django-modeltranslation, `description_rich` is translated into four columns (_xo, _uz, _ru, _en). In save(), only `self.description_rich` is sanitized — this resolves to the active-language column at the time of the call. When TranslationAdmin saves a Project, all four columns are written to the instance, but only the active-locale column goes through sanitize_rich_text(). The other three locale columns are persisted unsanitized and served publicly via the detail template.
suggested_fix:
In Project.save(), iterate all translated columns before calling super().save():
```python
for lang in ('xo', 'uz', 'ru', 'en'):
    field = f'description_rich_{lang}'
    val = getattr(self, field, None)
    if val:
        setattr(self, field, sanitize_rich_text(val))
```
Or import MODELTRANSLATION_LANGUAGES from settings to avoid hardcoding the language list.
verdict_note: Verified: translations.py confirms description_rich is in ProjectTranslation.fields. models.py line 107-108 only sanitizes self.description_rich (active locale). Real sanitization gap for non-active locale columns.

title: bleach css_sanitizer silently inactive: tinycss2 missing from requirements.txt
description: sanitize_rich_text() tries to import bleach.css_sanitizer.CSSSanitizer (which requires tinycss2). tinycss2 is not in requirements.txt (only bleach==6.2.0). The import fails silently and css_sanitizer is set to None. The else branch at line 47 also does nothing for bleach >= 6 (condition `int('6') < 6` is False). bleach then strips all style attribute values silently, meaning no inline CSS from TinyMCE is preserved — a permanent silent UX regression.
suggested_fix: Add 'tinycss2' to requirements.txt (or use 'bleach[css]' extra if available). On the server: venv/bin/pip install tinycss2. Also add a startup warning log when css_sanitizer is None so this degradation is visible in production logs rather than silently affecting all rich-text content.
verdict_note: Verified: requirements.txt has only bleach==6.2.0, no tinycss2. utils.py lines 24-28 has the try/except ImportError fallback to None. The else branch (line 47) is dead for bleach 6 since int('6') < 6 is False. Silent CSS stripping confirmed.

title: get_homepage_data evaluates get_featured_projects queryset twice — double DB hit
description: Line 91: `featured = self.repository.get_featured_projects()` returns a lazy QuerySet. Line 95: `if not featured` evaluates it (first DB hit). Then `featured` is passed as the dict value under 'featured_projects' — the template iterates it as a second DB hit. This is 2 DB calls where 1 suffices.
suggested_fix: Evaluate into a list once: `featured = list(self.repository.get_featured_projects())`. Both the truthiness check and template iteration then operate on the in-memory list at zero extra DB cost.
verdict_note: Verified: services.py lines 91-95 confirmed. get_featured_projects() returns a QuerySet (not a list). `if not featured` on line 95 evaluates it; the dict value at line 93 is the same unevaluated queryset object which the template evaluates again.

title: SiteSettings.load() bypasses the 5-minute cache in _apps_visible() and error handlers
description: _apps_visible() (line 86) and the custom 404/500 handlers (lines 34 and 46) call SiteSettings.load() directly. load() is a raw get_or_create(pk=1) — it always hits the database. The caching layer is SiteSettingsService.get(), which serves from a 5-minute in-memory cache. _apps_visible() is called on every request to Apps-guarded pages, adding an unnecessary uncached DB SELECT per dispatch.
suggested_fix: Replace SiteSettings.load() with SiteSettingsService.get() in _apps_visible() (line 86) and in the custom_404_view and custom_500_view handlers. The import `from core.services import SiteSettingsService` is available at the top of the file (line 15 of api/views.py; add to web/views.py if not present).
verdict_note: Verified: views.py lines 34, 46, 86 call SiteSettings.load() directly. services.py confirms SiteSettingsService.get() is the caching path. SiteSettings.load() is defined in core/services.py as get_or_create(pk=1) with no cache.

title: ProjectListSerializer.get_tech_tags slices bypass prefetch cache — N+1 on project list
description: get_tech_tags (line 58) calls obj.technologies.all()[:6] for every object in the list response. ProjectViewSet.get_queryset() does .prefetch_related('technologies'), but the [:6] slice creates a new QuerySet from the M2M descriptor and bypasses the prefetch cache entirely. Django's prefetch cache is only consumed by unsliced .all() calls. Each sliced call issues a fresh SELECT ... LIMIT 6, so a page of 10 projects produces 10 extra queries.
suggested_fix: Access the prefetch cache via unsliced .all(), then slice in Python: `return [t.name for t in list(obj.technologies.all())[:6]]`. The unsliced .all() hits the prefetch cache; the Python slice happens in memory with no DB round-trip.
verdict_note: Verified: serializers.py line 58 uses obj.technologies.all()[:6]. views.py line 45 confirms .prefetch_related('technologies') is present. Django prefetch cache bypass by sliced queryset is a documented behavior. Real N+1.

title: SiteSettingsSerializer._url methods use bare dict-key access self.context['request']
description: All five get_*_url methods call self._url(obj.field, self.context['request']) with bare key lookup. If SiteSettingsSerializer is ever instantiated without a request in context (management command, test, admin inline), a KeyError is raised. Sibling serializers (ProjectListSerializer, PostListSerializer) correctly use self.context.get('request').
suggested_fix: Use .get() at call sites: `self._url(obj.favicon, self.context.get('request'))`. Also guard in _url(): `if not field_value or not request: return None`.
verdict_note: Verified: serializers.py lines 142-154 all use self.context['request'] bare key. _url() method at line 136-139 does not guard against None request. The only current caller (SiteSettingsView) always passes request, so no current crash, but the pattern is fragile.

title: setup_rbac references removed 'botproxy' and 'osint' app labels silently producing incomplete RBAC
description: create_rbac_groups() queries for permissions by content_type__app_label='botproxy' (line 35) and content_type__app_label='osint' (line 42). Both apps were removed. The .first() + if perm guards prevent crashes, but running manage.py setup_rbac or the post-migrate signal produces an analyst group missing the intended botproxy/osint permissions with no warning. The analyst group gets only view_* permissions — silently incomplete vs documented intent.
suggested_fix: Remove the two dead stanzas (lines 33-45) for botproxy and osint permissions. Either replace with the actual analyst-level permissions that exist today (e.g. servermonitor read-only), or simplify the analyst group to view_* only and update the comment.
verdict_note: Verified: setup_rbac.py lines 33-45 reference botproxy and osint app labels. CLAUDE.md confirms osint and botproxy apps were removed from the portfolio (portfolio-only since 2026-05-31). Guards prevent crashes but RBAC is silently incomplete.

title: TgAppRouterView docstring documents dead osint deep-link patterns with no implementation
description: The TgAppRouterView docstring (lines 384-389) lists two deep-link patterns — osint-p-{id} and osint-e-{id} — that were part of the removed osint app. _resolve_target() has no startswith('osint-') branch, so any saved BotFather deep link using these prefixes silently falls through to the home page. This is a documentation-reality gap from the osint removal.
suggested_fix: Remove the osint-p-{id} and osint-e-{id} lines from the docstring. Add a comment noting that unknown start params fall back to home if that is the intended behavior.
verdict_note: Verified: views.py docstring lines 384-385 list osint patterns. _resolve_target() lines 436-471 has no osint branch. osint app removal confirmed in CLAUDE.md (portfolio-only since 2026-05-31).

title: select_related() with no arguments on Experience is a no-op
description: PortfolioRepository.get_all_experience() calls Experience.objects.select_related().order_by('-start_date'). Experience has no FK or OneToOne fields. select_related() with no arguments tells Django to follow all relations — but there are none, so this is a complete no-op. It misleads readers into thinking an optimization is in place when there is none.
suggested_fix: Drop the no-arg select_related() entirely: `Experience.objects.order_by('-start_date')`.
verdict_note: Verified: services.py line 67 has select_related() with no args. models.py Experience model has no FK or OneToOne fields — only CharField, TextField, ImageField, URLField, DateField, BooleanField. Confirmed no-op.

title: Post.save() sanitizes only the active-locale content_rich, leaving content_rich_uz/ru/en unsanitized
description: translations.py registers content_rich for all 4 locales, so modeltranslation creates content_rich_xo/_uz/_ru/_en DB columns. PostAdminForm (admin.py lines 31-36) attaches RichTextWidget to each locale column directly. Post.save() at line 62-63 only sanitizes self.content_rich, which is the virtual accessor that resolves to whichever locale is active at save time (xo by default in Uzbek context). The three other locale columns receive raw TinyMCE HTML with no bleach pass. An admin user can inject arbitrary HTML/script into the English or Russian content fields and have it rendered via |safe in blog_detail.html.
suggested_fix: In Post.save(), iterate over all translated columns before calling super(): for lang_code in ('xo', 'uz', 'ru', 'en'): field = f'content_rich_{lang_code}'; val = getattr(self, field, None); if val: setattr(self, field, sanitize_rich_text(val)). Remove the existing single-field guard. This replaces 2 lines with 4 lines.
verdict_note: Confirmed by reading translations.py (content_rich in PostTranslation.fields), admin.py (RichTextWidget on each locale column), and models.py (save() only touches self.content_rich). Real XSS vector on multi-locale posts.

title: Public blog detail API leaks admin email address via nested UserSerializer
description: PostViewSet (views.py line 87) sets permission_classes = [permissions.AllowAny]. For all actions except list it returns PostSerializer, which nests UserSerializer (fields = ('id', 'username', 'email', 'bio', 'profile_picture')). Any anonymous GET /api/posts/<id>/ returns the author's email in the JSON response. Since the only publisher is the portfolio owner/admin, this exposes the admin account email publicly. UserSerializer was designed for the admin-only UserViewSet context; it was carried into the public serializer without trimming.
suggested_fix: Add a minimal public-safe nested serializer: class PostAuthorSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer): class Meta: model = User; fields = ('username', 'bio', 'profile_picture'). Use it in PostSerializer instead of UserSerializer. This removes email and id from the public surface while preserving display information.
verdict_note: Confirmed: views.py line 87 AllowAny + line 89-92 returns PostSerializer for detail; serializers.py line 81 nests full UserSerializer including email. User model (AbstractUser) confirmed to have username and email fields.

title: tinycss2 missing from requirements.txt — bleach silently zeros all inline CSS on every save
description: sanitize_rich_text imports CSSSanitizer inside try/except ImportError. tinycss2 is not in requirements.txt. In the project venv, the import fails with 'No module named tinycss2', so css_sanitizer = None. Because bleach==6.2.0, the major-version fallback (int('6') < 6) is False, so the 'styles' kwarg is also never passed. bleach.clean() receives ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES with '*': ['style', ...] but no css_sanitizer — bleach 6 zeroes all inline style attributes to style="" (verified empirically: '<span style="color:red">' becomes '<span style="">'). Every TinyMCE post saved through the admin loses all inline styling silently.
suggested_fix: Add tinycss2>=1.2 to requirements.txt. It is already a transitive dependency of bleach 6 but is not pinned directly. After redeploy, the try branch succeeds, CSSSanitizer is constructed, and inline styles are properly validated against ALLOWED_STYLES instead of being zeroed.
verdict_note: Confirmed by reading requirements.txt (no tinycss2 entry), running import test in project venv (ImportError confirmed), and testing bleach.clean() output in venv (style= zeroed to empty string).

title: PostListSerializer.reading_time defeats .defer('content_rich') causing N+1 queries on the API list
description: PostViewSet.get_queryset() calls .defer('content_rich') for the list action (views.py line 105). PostViewSet.get_serializer_class() returns PostListSerializer for the list action (line 91). PostListSerializer.Meta.fields includes 'reading_time' (serializers.py line 99). Post.reading_time is a @property that calls strip_tags(self.content_rich) (models.py line 57). Accessing the deferred field triggers a separate SELECT per Post row. On a page of 10 posts this is 10 extra round-trips inside synchronous Gunicorn workers, defeating the purpose of the defer entirely.
suggested_fix: Either (a) remove 'reading_time' from PostListSerializer.Meta.fields — the list cards don't need it since the detail SSR view renders it server-side; or (b) add reading_time = models.PositiveSmallIntegerField(default=1) to Post, compute it in save() before super(), and remove the @property. verdict_note: Confirmed: models.py line 54-59 shows @property reading_time accessing self.content_rich; serializers.py line 99 includes reading_time in PostListSerializer fields; views.py line 104-105 defers content_rich only for list action while line 91 returns PostListSerializer for list.

title: defer('content_rich') in three list querysets is a no-op due to modeltranslation per-locale columns

title: API contact endpoint bypasses ContactService and all spam protection
description: ContactMessageViewSet (line 110) is a plain ModelViewSet with no perform_create override. POST /api/contact/ goes directly to serializer.save() → ContactMessage.objects.create(), completely bypassing ContactService.send_contact_message(). Result: no confirmation email to submitter, no notification to site owner. Additionally, is_honeypot_filled and is_rate_limited from spam_protection.py are never called on this path. The SSR ContactView.post (presentation/web/views.py:331) correctly applies both guards and calls ContactService; the DRF endpoint does neither. A bot can POST directly to /api/contact/ at unlimited rate.
suggested_fix:
Override perform_create in ContactMessageViewSet to delegate to ContactService and apply rate limiting:

    from contact.services import ContactRepository, ContactService
    from contact.spam_protection import is_rate_limited
    from rest_framework.exceptions import Throttled

    def perform_create(self, serializer):
        if is_rate_limited(self.request):
            raise Throttled()
        data = serializer.validated_data
        ContactService(ContactRepository()).send_contact_message(
            data['name'], data['email'], data['subject'], data['message']
        )
        # Do NOT call serializer.save() separately — ContactService.repository.create_message() already does the DB write.
verdict_note: Confirmed. ContactMessageViewSet has no perform_create override (verified: grep returns no output). ContactService is never called on the API path. spam_protection functions are not imported or referenced in api/views.py. Findings 1, 4, and 9 are triplicate reports of the same root cause — merged into one.

title: ContactView.post has no exception handling around send_contact_message — DB error returns 500
description: ContactView.post calls contact_service.send_contact_message() at line 354-355 with no try/except. ContactService.send_contact_message() calls ContactRepository.create_message() which is a raw ContactMessage.objects.create(). The email helpers use fail_silently=True so those don't propagate, but the DB write does — any connection loss or constraint violation propagates uncaught through TemplateView.post() and surfaces as HTTP 500. The user gets an error page instead of a friendly message.
verdict_note: Confirmed. Lines 354-355 contain an unguarded service call. ContactRepository.create_message() is a raw .objects.create() with no exception handling (services.py line 12). Email sends use fail_silently=True so only the DB write is unguarded. Severity lowered from high to medium: DB failures are rare and transient; the impact is a 500 page, not data loss or security breach.

title: Non-atomic rate-limit counter allows burst bypass under concurrency
description: is_rate_limited() does cache.get(key, 0) then cache.set(key, current+1, ...) as two separate non-atomic operations (lines 40 and 47). Under Gunicorn with 3 sync workers, two concurrent requests from the same IP can both read current=0, both pass the limit check, and both set it to 1 — effectively letting them both through. With Redis the race window is small but real; cache.incr is atomic while get+set is not.
suggested_fix:
Use atomic increment via cache.add + cache.incr (atomic on Redis):

    def is_rate_limited(request) -> bool:
        ip = _get_client_ip(request)
        key = f"{RATE_LIMIT_KEY_PREFIX}{ip}"
        cache.add(key, 0, RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS)  # no-op if key exists
        count = cache.incr(key)  # atomic on Redis; returns new value
        if count > RATE_LIMIT_MAX_SUBMISSIONS:
            logger.warning('Rate-limit hit for IP %s (%d/%d)', ip, count, RATE_LIMIT_MAX_SUBMISSIONS)
            return True
        return False

Note: LocMemCache.incr raises ValueError if key doesn't exist — the cache.add(key, 0, ...) call before it prevents that.
verdict_note: Confirmed. Lines 40-47 are exactly as described: cache.get then cache.set, two separate calls with no atomicity. Findings 3 and 6 are duplicate reports of the same bug — merged into one.

title: X-Forwarded-For spoofing allows rate-limit bypass
description: _get_client_ip takes xff.split(',')[0] (line 55) — the leftmost XFF value. Nginx is configured with proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for (jaysonkhan.conf lines 227/237/252/262/274), which APPENDS the real IP to any XFF the client already sent. A bot sending X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4 produces header 1.2.3.4, <real-ip> by the time it reaches Django; the code reads 1.2.3.4 as the key. The attacker rotates fake leftmost IPs to evade the 3/10-min limit entirely. Nginx already sets X-Real-IP: $remote_addr (verified: jaysonkhan.conf lines 226/237/251/262/273) which is the actual socket IP and not client-spoofable. The same vulnerable helper is duplicated in presentation/web/views.py HomeView._get_client_ip (line 134).
verdict_note: Confirmed. spam_protection.py line 55 reads xff.split(',')[0]. Nginx jaysonkhan.conf uses $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for (verified lines 227/237/252/262/274) which appends rather than overwriting. X-Real-IP: $remote_addr is set on every proxy block (lines 226/237/251/262/273). The spoofing bypass is real and trivially exploitable.

The result: is_read has no write path anywhere — not in admin, not in the service layer, not via a signal or admin action. Every message stays is_read=False forever. core/dashboard.py lines 22 and 128 query ContactMessage.objects.filter(is_read=False).count() for the inbox unread count badge — that count never decrements, making the dashboard unread indicator permanently inflated.

Remove is_read from readonly_fields so Unfold admin renders it as a checkbox on the change page. Optionally add a list action to bulk-mark-as-read:

    # is_read is intentionally NOT in readonly_fields so it can be toggled

For a better UX, also add a custom admin action:

    @admin.action(description='Mark selected as read')
    def mark_as_read(self, request, queryset):
        queryset.update(is_read=True)

    actions = [mark_as_read]
verdict_note: Confirmed. admin.py line 12 lists readonly_fields as all the content fields plus created_at. is_read is in list_display and list_filter but has no write path. Grepping all backend Python files for is_read shows zero .update(is_read=...) or .save() calls. dashboard.py lines 22 and 128 query unread count — it is permanently the total count.

description: log_contact_message builds the Telegram notification button URL at line 292 as f'{self._domain}/{admin_prefix}contact/contactmessage/'. admin_prefix is obtained via getattr(settings, 'ADMIN_URL_PREFIX', 'admin/'). title: Comment.text allows empty string on image-only comments, violating model intent
description: Comment.text is declared as TextField(max_length=1000) with no blank=True and no default. The AddCommentView allows the request through when `not text and image`, then creates the comment with text='' (views.py line 363). Model.save() skips Django field validators, so the empty string is written to PostgreSQL silently. This violates the model's stated intent, produces __str__ returning 'display_name: ' for every image-only comment, and makes the admin list look broken. The secondary duplicate-detection claim in the original finding is incorrect: the actual code at views.py line 358 has `if last_comment and text and last_comment.text == text`, and the `and text` guard short-circuits correctly for image-only comments.
suggested_fix: Add blank=True to Comment.text: `text = models.TextField(max_length=1000, blank=True, default='')`. No duplicate-detection change needed — the existing guard is correct.

title: TelegramAuthView GET failure returns JSON instead of redirect in browser popup flow
description: TelegramAuthView.get() is the Telegram Login Widget redirect callback — opened in a browser popup. On HMAC failure, line 110 returns JsonResponse({'error': '...'}, status=400). The browser popup shows raw JSON with no recovery path. The class docstring explicitly states it 'stores session, then redirects', implying all paths should redirect. The AJAX path (TelegramLoginView) correctly returns JSON because JavaScript consumes it, but this GET-redirect path is rendered directly in the browser.

TelegramAuthView (views.py line 114) calls `TelegramEntity.get_or_create_with_source(flat)` with no surrounding try/except, so a tampered or malformed id propagates as an unhandled ValueError or KeyError, yielding a Django 500 error page. By contrast, TelegramLoginView (views.py lines 154-158) wraps the same call in try/except Exception and returns a 500 JSON response gracefully. The inconsistency creates an unhandled exception path through TelegramAuthView.

Then wrap the call at TelegramAuthView line 114 in the same try/except pattern used in TelegramLoginView.

title: Admin user email exposed via public PostViewSet detail endpoint
description: PostViewSet (presentation/api/views.py line 87) sets permission_classes = [AllowAny]. Its list action uses the lightweight PostListSerializer (no author field), but the retrieve (detail) action uses PostSerializer, which embeds the full UserSerializer. UserSerializer exposes fields = ('id', 'username', 'email', 'bio', 'profile_picture'). Any unauthenticated visitor can GET /api/posts/{id}/ and read the admin user's email address and profile picture path. The email is the login credential for the custom User model and the JWT /api/token/ endpoint.
suggested_fix: Create a minimal `PublicAuthorSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer)` with only a display name field (e.g. `fields = ('username',)` or a computed `display_name`). Override the author field in PostSerializer: `author = PublicAuthorSerializer(read_only=True)`. Keep UserSerializer only for admin-gated contexts.

title: X-Forwarded-For spoofing bypasses AdminIPRestrictionMiddleware and contact rate limit
description: Both AdminIPRestrictionMiddleware._get_ip() (lines 141-145) and contact/spam_protection._get_client_ip() (lines 51-56) extract the client IP as xff.split(',')[0].strip() — the leftmost, client-controlled entry. Nginx uses proxy_add_x_forwarded_for (confirmed in security/nginx/jaysonkhan.conf lines 227/239/253/275), which APPENDS the real peer IP to whatever the client sends, rather than replacing it. An attacker who sends `X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1` will have Nginx forward `X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1, <real_ip>`. Django reads 127.0.0.1 as the client IP, bypassing the admin allowlist entirely. The same flaw in spam_protection allows the contact rate limit to be defeated by cycling spoofed XFF values.
suggested_fix: Use REMOTE_ADDR directly in AdminIPRestrictionMiddleware._get_ip() — Nginx sets this to the actual TCP socket peer and it cannot be spoofed by a client: `return request.META.get('REMOTE_ADDR', '0.0.0.0')`. For spam_protection, either use REMOTE_ADDR or, if there are multiple trusted proxies, use the last untrusted entry: `parts = xff.split(','); return parts[-2].strip() if len(parts) >= 2 else parts[0].strip()`.
verdict_note: Confirmed by reading security_middleware.py lines 141-145, spam_protection.py lines 51-56, and nginx/jaysonkhan.conf lines 227 and 275 (`proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`). Nginx appends; Django reads leftmost; bypass is trivially exploitable.

title: User model missing USERNAME_FIELD='email' despite docstring claiming email is the auth identifier
description: The User model inherits AbstractUser and adds a unique email field, but never sets USERNAME_FIELD = 'email' or REQUIRED_FIELDS = []. Django's default USERNAME_FIELD is 'username', so the admin login form shows a 'username' prompt, and the JWT /api/token/ endpoint at urls.py line 41 authenticates by username, not email — contrary to the docstring which says 'email is the unique identifier for authentication'. Any code that calls authenticate(email=...) (e.g. a future login form or custom backend) will silently fail. The __str__ returns self.username, which will be an empty string for users created without a username in programmatic flows.
suggested_fix: Add `USERNAME_FIELD = 'email'` and `REQUIRED_FIELDS = []` to the User class. Change `__str__` to return `self.email`. Consider making `username` nullable (`blank=True, null=True`) to make the intent clear, and create a custom UserManager that omits the username requirement.
verdict_note: Confirmed: models.py has no USERNAME_FIELD or REQUIRED_FIELDS override. AbstractUser defaults to username. urls.py line 41 wires TokenObtainPairView which uses the USERNAME_FIELD to authenticate. The email-based auth docstring is misleading and the JWT endpoint will reject email-based credentials.

Add a comment explaining what was removed and why.
